statement: A box holds $6$ red, $6$ blue, $4$ green and $2$ yellow pencils. Without looking, Tariq takes pencils out of the box one at a time. What is the least number of pencils he must take to be certain that he has at least $3$ pencils of the same color?

choices.misconception: I forgot about the yellow pencils and used 2 pencils of each of 3 colors plus one more, 2 x 3 + 1 = 7.
I took 2 pencils of each of the 4 colors but forgot that one more pencil is needed to force a third of some color.
I thought I needed 3 pencils of each of the 4 colors, so I multiplied 3 x 4 = 12.
I made sure of getting 3 red pencils, taking all 6 blue, 4 green and 2 yellow first, 12 + 3 = 15. Any color is allowed.

hints: Think about the unluckiest way the draws could go.
How many pencils can Tariq hold without having $3$ of any one color?
He can hold at most $2$ of each of the $4$ colors, which is $8$ pencils. What happens with the next one?

solutions.reliable: Tariq can hold $8$ pencils with no $3$ of the same color: $2$ red, $2$ blue, $2$ green and $2$ yellow. So $8$ pencils are not enough. With $9$ pencils, if every color appeared at most twice he would have at most $2 \times 4 = 8$ pencils, which is impossible, so some color appears at least $3$ times. The answer is $9$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
